steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Granny? Didn't you say you'd be back late tonight?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Oh, come on now, don't give me the silent treatment. I feel like I've done something wrong here.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Oh, it's you, Stan.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: S-Sorry, I, err, wasn't trying to scare you or anything...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: It's fine, it's fine. Lighten up.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Say, isn't this the first time you've dropped over to mine?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Have a sit and I'll whip you up a snack. You're fine with tangerine fizzy drinks, yeah? Help yourself. As for that snack...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I've brought something.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Nice. Let's see... Fried fin and potato pie? Bit more of a meal than a snack, no?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: ...I made it myself.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Suppose I'll have a try, then.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Get me a can as well while you're at it!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: No, not over there, under the kitchen cupboard where we put the brooms!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: *glug* *glug*... Man, that taste...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Me Da said he'd rather chew on his welding rod than eat my cooking.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: The flavor is a tad bit... intense.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Help me out here, Feist. Don't doom the boys at the factory to eat this day after day.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: As you know, I ain't got any talents other than learning how to weld from me Da. I was just waiting to be let into his team. He's discussed it all with the factory director already.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Wait, don't tell me...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Last month, they went on an 'optimization' spree at the assembly line all for the sake of 'improving our manufacturing efficiency', so me Da got 'optimized' to the cafeteria—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: No way!

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Now, I'm slated to join his team there, but even after half a month's worth of practice at home, I can't even get the simplest thing done in the kitchen, let alone cook anything edible.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Me Da's about to retire, Feist, and I'd rather not get kicked out of the cafeteria then fired from the factory the moment he's gone.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: That optimization plan was my idea...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: It was?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Nah, I don't blame you. When you were little, you were already talking about how you wanted to get the whole factory modernized. You managed to put your money where your mouth is, unlike me...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Anyhow, since you were the one who came up with it, d'you think you could change it back? Put me Da back on the assembly line?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'm not sure the director would be too happy to do it... but we'd better go see him, just in case.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Worst comes to worst, I could ask around and see if any other lines need a welder.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I-If you could?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Just leave it to me.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: So, what'd the director say, Feist?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: You don't look too good. Don't tell me—No, don't tell me the director... Was he... mad?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Nah. You should've seen that why-should-I give-a-damn-about-anyone-else look on his face... I almost couldn't help but stuff your fried fin down his gob.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: He insists there's no going back. As for the assembly line, he says he sent your dad to the cafeteria because there were no vacancies at the factory in the first place.

spans.text: He insists there's no going back. As for the assembly line, he says he sent your dad to the cafeteria
there were no vacancies at the factory in the first place.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Damn. Me Da's been all over Highbury the last few days, says a real big manufacturer went bankrupt recently. Not even the lads with experience can find work. A wet-behind-the-ears guy like me... No factory's going to want me.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: You could try something outside a factory. Maybe try your hand at business? Start a small grocery, something like that?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Or maybe the railway? I'm not too familiar with them, not sure if they're recruiting.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Or, err, even dormitory cleaner's not a bad job. It's hard work, but at least you'll be paid...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'm the one who got you into this mess, so it's my responsibility to get you out. Come on, let's head home and change into something nicer. We'll set out and look for work in the afternoon.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: ...Not a single bite.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'll jot down the places we hit up today. We can try our luck in some other borough tomorrow.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Damn bloody pen's dried up... Dammit!

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: How about we just call it here, Feist.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Like I said, I can't blame you for this. Technology marches on, and even if you weren't around, the director would've 'optimized' some people out eventually.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Talented guys like you can find their place no matter how tech develops, but people like me... We're not the same.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I don't have any work experience or book smarts, my family's got no money, and I'm not a people person like you, able to get along with everyone...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Don't be so hard on yourself, Stan. We were just unlucky today.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: But we've already scoured all of Highbury, and Auchterigg too—

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: Why so glum, chaps? Worried about how to pay your bills? Not happy with your work? Or maybe you got let off by one of the Highbury factories?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: And who might you be, Mister...?

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: I'm a recruiter. Interested?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: That's great! Recruiting for what?

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: Well, what line of work are you two in?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Welding.

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: Welders are just what we need. C'mon, I'll show you our factory.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Where is it? We've spent the whole day checking every single one in Highbury and none of them needed welders. Is it just opened?

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: Err, yeah.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: In Magna Borough maybe? We were going to try our luck there tomorrow.

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: Sure enough, that's the place—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Opening a factory in a posh borough like that? You tell a good joke, mister. Let's go, Stan.
A damp, warm night breeze blows through Highbury from a corner beyond the streetlamp's reach, causing them to shiver.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I'll be heading home, I guess.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: And then?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I dunno. Me Da's pension isn't enough to keep himself fed. I know he wants to take care of me, but we'll both starve if he does...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Sorry Feist, you don't need to listen to my bellyaching. You've done enough.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I'm just going to go back to the factory and join the cafeteria. I should be able to muddle my way through.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Back to the factory... Join the cafeteria...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: That might just work out.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Glad you agree—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: No, Stan. I'm not letting you give up here. Like I said, this is my responsibility.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: If you can't cook, then I'll take your place.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: What about your work?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: You can handle it, optimizing lines and suchlike.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Are you serious?!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Better than slaving away in a kitchen, am I right?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I-I dunno, I really don't have any talent like you do...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: If you don't give it a try, how do you know you're not talented at it?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'll talk things over with Granny and the director. Give it a shot, won't you?

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Swap positions? I don't know what's gotten into your heads. What does your grandmother think, Feist? Is she really alright with this lunacy?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: If she wasn't, I wouldn't be here talking with you.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Heaven knows why you're being so stubborn about this... Forget it.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Very well then, swap positions. But mark my words, there can be no disruptions to either the assembly line or the cafeteria. If there's any trouble, it'll be you two bearing the consequences.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: W-Will we be fired?

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: A firing would be the least of your troubles. If anything happens, you'll be compensating for our losses in full!

spans.text: A firing would be the least of your troubles. If anything happens, you'll be compensating for our losses

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Feist? Is that really you?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: 'Tis.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: The director told me all about it yesterday. I thought it was just you youngsters up to some nonsense.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Since you two are serious, I won't coddle you. Do what needs to be done, and don't make a mess of things. Got that?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Good. Now get those baskets of potatoes peeled.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: You're quite the neat peeler—Wait, how come so many of these little potatoes only have a single cut? Been testing one of your 'inventions' again?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Ahaha...

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: I don't care how you get them peeled, but you need to clean up your own mess.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Will do. No need to worry, sir.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Seems like I need to do some more troubleshooting—

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I-I've got a bit of a situation on my hands here, Feist, and I really dunno how to fix it. I've got to ask you something.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: No problem, ask away.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: It's about belt B7... Seems like it's running slower than the belts further down the line...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Slower? Might be something jamming it. Did you go through the entire pre-startup inspection?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I-I did it all like the manual said...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: How about the drive motors?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I'll have a look—Oh, there really was...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: As long as you managed to find the issue. If there's anything else, just call.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Idle hands, Feist! I could hear you chattering away on the walkie-talkie!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I-I'll be done real quick!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Let's try turning the angle of the blade a bit...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: All peeled! Passing them over now, sir—

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Hold on a second, let me take a look...

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: You sure are something, Feist. Standardizing the size of the potatoes? Is this how you cook at home?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Well, at home it's just me and Granny, but here in the cafeteria we're feeding an entire factory. I thought it'd be more efficient this way.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: And if you look here, I was tinkering with this potato-cutting machine last night. As long as the potatoes are all the same size—

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Alright, I heard enough! So what about the bits of the potato the machine lopped off? Just going to throw them away?

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Since it's still your first day, peel a few more potatoes to make up for the extra waste. And make sure you use a normal knife this time!

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Hmm, these one's aren't half-bad.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Once I teach you how to fry the fins, I'll be making the potato pies, so chop chop—Another one of your infernal contraptions? Going to use it to debone the fins?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Well, more than just debone—

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Don't bother, we use frozen fillets here. It's not as tricky as you think.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Here's how you batter them. I'll only show you once, so remember it well.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Feist—

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Put that communicator down. If you keep dawdling, the entire factory'll starve.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Yes, sir...

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Remember what I said about the flour blend? Half all-purpose, half self-rising... Right, just like that.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Wait! Don't beat those yolks into the batter! How are you going to get your foam afterwards?

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: ...Forget it, just mix it all together and get those fillets covered. Surely you know how to fry it—Don't just put something wet into a deep-fryer! The hell do you cook at home?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Stewed veggies and the like.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: *sigh* Never mind. Not like I've got enough oil in my own home to deep-fry things myself.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Finally, it's done. Let me have a taste—

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: Eurgh! How did you manage to make them taste so raw?

spans.text: Eurgh! How did you manage to make them taste so

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: What's the time right now—Oh, bollocks.

steps.name: Cafeteria Manager
steps.text: I don't have the time to walk you through everything again, so I'll write the instructions down. Please follow them step by step, alright?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: How's things on your end, Stan? What did you call me for earlier?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: The production line's sorta... stopped...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Stopped?!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Wait right there, I'm coming over!

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: One volunteer in the cafeteria, and of the fried fins he prepared for the factory men, a quarter was burnt, a quarter was raw, and the last half was left forgotten to stink up the kitchen.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: As for our other volunteer, he might have an even more impressive record: Insufficient pre-startup inspections and an inability to resolve issues when they came up, giving our workers half a day off thanks to the paralyzed lines.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Remember how I told you boys you would be bearing the consequences?

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: No need to come in tomorrow, Stan. You'll need the time to sort your life out.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Director, this was all my idea—

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Don't think you're off the hook. It was his mess, but you're responsible. You get back to optimizing the lines. Today's losses are coming out of your wages, mind.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: You can forget seeing another penny from me for the rest of the year.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: How could you even think of something like that?!

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Oho, still have some vim and vigor in you?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: The line stoppage was my fault, so I'll pay the cost! Wouldn't Feist paying for the fins be enough?

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Pay? With what money? Your father's pension?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Director.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Ah, Catherine, you're here. Take your grandson home already so you can teach him not to cause so much trouble.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Don't worry, Feist is a clever kid. He doesn't need reminding when he needs to learn something. I'm here to talk about other business.

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: Hmph. These two have caused quite the ruckus in this factory. What more is there to talk about?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I don't remember you looking like this when I came to chat with you a while ago.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Granny?

steps.name: Factory Director
steps.text: *cough*!

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Take Stan back to ours, Feist. I've got quite a few things to discuss with the director here.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Granny—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: The director gave in. Feist, you can go back to the line, and Stan can go back to the cafeteria. The two of you will be docked a month's wages.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I managed to put a good word in with him earlier, but I suppose he's still rather pissed off at the two of you.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Since he's being like that, I had no choice but to mention a few sketchy things we noticed that the public didn't.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Sorry, Granny...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Don't apologize to me, apologize to the boys in the factory tomorrow.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: And here, your fried fins. The cafeteria packed them up for you.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You fried them, you eat them. I don't care what state they were in, they weren't off when you dipped them in the fryer.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I'll be off now. You two, think long and hard about what you'll be doing next.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: *sigh*

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Feeling peckish, Stan?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: ...A tad.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Man, it still stinks even after it cooled down... We should find somewhere else to talk—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Let's head to the lift platform. We can find somewhere high up and stargaze a bit.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Hff—haaaah... Been a while since I climbed so high.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Yeah, it's a lot comfier here than in the workshop.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I've never really thought so.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Figured you'd say that.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Say what?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: When I was inspecting everything this morning, I saw all the little notes you left behind.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Things like 'Two loops here, no more' or 'To Sam: don't forget the corners and gaps when cleaning'. The handwriting's a bit carefree, and some of them even have a little smiley face at the end.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Even if I knew the entire line in and out, I wouldn't be able to bring myself to draw one of those. I just can't smile down there.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I wasn't smiling much in the cafeteria either.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Suppose I better start getting these fried fins down.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: They rotten?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: No, but they stink to high heaven.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'll have a bite, then.
The two of them each nibble on a piece of fried fin.

The nauseating scent of burnt batter and raw fin is blown away by the night wind, and to the two young men who had not eaten all afternoon out of nervousness, even cold fin fillets carried a hint of appetizing aroma.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Not sure if you still remember, but there was one time you lead us younger kids up here, and we spent the entire night playing together. The next day, everyone got a right trashing when we went home.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Of course I remember. Granny was furious, since I was the leader and all.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: We talked about what we wanted to do when we grew up. You were the first one to speak up. You said the factories were driving Londinium into the future, and you wanted to be the guy driving the factories.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: You said there'd be a day when machines would do all the work for us. We'd just need to pop into the office, press a few buttons, then call it a day—

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Er, did I say something wrong?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: No, it's just that even after all the effort I put in, we're actually further away from that dream than before.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Granny was right. I'm too immature. All I could think about was how to make things more efficient, and along the way, I forgot what kind of place a factory actually is.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: If there really does come a day we could just push a few buttons, why would a factory need to hire so many people?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: *sigh* If I wasn't so optimization-obsessed, you'd be a fine welder right now.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Maybe not. Truth be told, I don't really want to be a welder.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Y-You don't?

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: We grew up in the factories, so we all know what a factory man's life is like.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: You either stand at the line the entire day, or you're clambering up and down the machines to service them. People think you make parts, or weld pipes, but you actually never get to see your own result.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: The only time I really wanted to be a factory man was the time a lady manning the lathe gave me a perfectly round ball she made out of some scrap metal.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: But most of the time, her works just went right down the belt before I could even make out their shape. Just parts of one big process in the end.
In the distant factory district, the night shift disembarks from the railway carriages, while the day shift trickle out of the countless factories of Highbury after a hard day's work.
The workers seem nothing compared to the giant buildings behind them.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: You can see the factory as a whole. You know what everyone's work actually means. That's why I say you've got talent and I don't.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: You know which bit of the finished product you made yourself and what it does, even if the parts have nothing to do with us once they leave the factory...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: But I can't do that. To me, factory work's a job where you never get to see the fruits of your labor. You just make the same thing day after day for some cash.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: The factory won't let go of you, but me? I'm just a welding rod to them. A lousy one, 'just like burnt fins,' according to me Da. They'd throw me away without a second thought.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I know there's nothing wrong with it, really. I'm just not used to factory work.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Back when we were little, I never said what I wanted to be when I grew up, because I didn't know.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I just want to do something that I can see through from start to end... Something I can...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Something I can point at when I'm off the clock and proudly tell people: 'You see this? I did that!' ...Something like that.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: I don't care what it is. A chair, a set of knives, a sick guy who got better under my care, even a burdenbeast raised by myself...

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: But I was born to a factory man, and so I should be a welder. Because that's what me Da is.
The railcars tug on their whistles as they take the workers clocking out back to their dorms, like the whinnies of a burdenbeast.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: He'll be back home soon. We should go.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Wait, Stan. There's... There's some things I still don't get.

steps.name: Stan
steps.text: Afraid there's no time for that.
After heading down the platform, Feist returns home, looking over the blueprints he was so proud of once more.
He had always thought of the factory as a whole. It's how his granny does it, so he thought that's how others would too.
But as it turns out, not so.
He thinks of the time he was handling those last few potatoes in the kitchen. He didn't have the least idea what they would become, nor did he really care.
He feels like his impression of the kitchen is more or less the same as Stan's impression of the factory. Maybe even a little better, actually.
At least fried fins and potato pies would make their way back into his belly eventually. But a factory's products? The workers don't have anything to do with them.
Maybe he could drive the factory into the future some day, but what about the workers like Stan, the ones who don't want to do fruitless tasks forever and ever, without knowing anything else?
Workers like Stan who wouldn't even get the chance to work a never-ending job?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Stop the finished parts on the line for a bit? No, if every segment stopped, the total time lost would be unacceptable.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Maybe.. make the line out of transparent materials? Though I'm not sure anywhere even has that technology, let alone the cost...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Or maybe some sort of handover process once the goods are leaving the factory that involves all the workers?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: That damn factory director would have to sign off on it, though. No, it's got to be something to do with the line itself...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: What's wrong with me today? Why can't I think of anything that'll work? There's got to be a way—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Oh, Granny...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Us night shifters just clocked out. Why're you not asleep yet?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Blueprints? You thinking of getting Stan back on the line?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Do you really know what he wants?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: He wants... to make something he can see the end product of. Something he can point at when he's off the clock and say that it's his work.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: And you're helping him do this?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I'm trying my best.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Good, I'm glad you didn't cause such a ruckus for nothing.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: But this isn't something you can do with a few late nights. Stay calm and take it easy. You've got more time left than me to see it through.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Also, I was just talking to Stan's father. Stan's decided to leave Highbury. Leave Londinium, even.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: What's he—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Apparently, he wants to try his luck in some nearby villages, see if he can raise some burdenbeasts.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Go get some sleep, Feist.
Catherine's tone is firm, and Feist can feel the sleepiness building up behind his brow.
He drags his worn body to his bed and flings himself on it, falling into slumber as the sun rises behind his curtains.

He dreams of Stan mounting a burdenbeast, a treasured companion he raised from a calf. He sits astride the beast's wide back, and with one great leap off the top of the building, he rides off away from the city.
As for Feist himself? He waves farewell, then turns back to Londinium, back into his workshop.
